feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy/operations leadership. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, tighter consolidation of overlapping skills sections, and a few consistency edits.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions at one organization show growth, trust, and increasing leadership scope.  
- Strong relevance and breadth: combines strategy, web/CMS, analytics, editorial systems, and multimedia in a way that fits senior digital communications roles well.  
- Generally strong writing: concise, professional, and easy to follow, with no obvious misspellings and very few grammatical issues.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities more than outcomes. Include measurable impact where possible (engagement growth, email performance, efficiency gains, cost savings, campaign results).  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap significantly. Consolidating these would improve structure and save space.  
- Fix stylistic inconsistencies: use serial commas consistently (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs later lists), standardize hyphenation (“cross-channel”/“Multi-channel”), and consider “12 years of experience” instead of “12 years experience.” Also make bullet formatting consistent, as some entries read like paragraph-plus-dashes.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and foregrounding leadership in digital transformation would increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, standard phrasing.
- Lead with your strongest differentiators: digital strategy leadership, platform modernization, and mission-driven/public-sector communications.
- Replace broad terms like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with “multi-channel digital communications” to reduce listiness.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving multi-channel communications, platform modernization, and content operations for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, editorial workflow design, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible messaging. Strong background in advocacy communications, cross-functional leadership, and building scalable systems that improve digital performance.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/systems language overlap with Core Competencies.
- “Advocacy messaging” and stakeholder coordination are reinforced repeatedly in Work Experience and Soft Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the summary, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the wording and making the categories more distinctive will improve scan value.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and tighten wording: “Digital strategy & transformation • Cross-channel communications • Web platform & CMS management • Editorial operations & governance • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Workflow architecture & automation • Stakeholder alignment & cross-functional collaboration • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, video & live event production”
- Replace “Multi-channel communication” with “Cross-channel communications” for more natural phrasing and consistency with the header.
- Consider swapping “Web & CMS administration” for “Web platform & CMS management,” which sounds more senior and strategic.
- If space allows, add one more differentiator tied to recent work, such as “AI-enabled search & structured content design.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header and Topline Skills; keep it high-level and avoid listing tools or detailed technical terms already covered elsewhere.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear scope and good technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around 3–5 high-impact outcomes and add scale/results to distinguish it from your NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital strategy, Drupal campaign delivery, content operations, and enterprise web improvements.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one outcome-focused line: “Built cross-channel workflows, governance standards, and analytics systems to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/CMS work more results-oriented: mention number of sites/pages, users, campaign launches, turnaround time, or stakeholder groups supported.
- Recast the AI bullet as a flagship achievement: “Led AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content modeling, and user discovery experience.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance,” “analytics,” and “enterprise web improvement” overlap with the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize what is new here (consulting scope, AI search, campaign builds).
- The footer project examples already cover microsites and AI search, so avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground enterprise outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget for a high-volume public-sector communications operation.”
- Combine web modernization into one impact bullet: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based; add metrics if available: email growth/open rates, social engagement, video output, event reach, cost savings, or production turnaround.
- Tighten ops/analytics bullets: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio…” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve leadership visibility and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version focused on enterprise oversight and results.
- Video/programming language also echoes older NACo entries; emphasize studio buildout and organizational capacity, not recurring production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item is too close to the adjacent NACo roles and reads as support-oriented rather than ownership-driven. Tighten it around scope, channel leadership, and systems/process impact.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Combine overlapping bullets and sharpen verbs: “Owned four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague process language with a clearer systems angle: “Built stronger editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and content consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role and the footer project; keep focus here on scaling/owning it, not originating video broadly.
- “Publishing workflows” and “coordination” also appear in the Director role; avoid repeating governance language too heavily.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tighter, more distinctive, and framed around leadership scope rather than repeating generic capability labels.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, differentiated terms: “Enterprise digital strategy” → “Enterprise web and content strategy”; “Multi-channel communications leadership” → “Cross-channel digital operations leadership.”
- Add governance/operating-model language that signals seniority: “Editorial governance and publishing operations” is stronger than “Editorial systems and governance.”
- Tighten audience/messaging phrasing: “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” → “Public-sector, membership, and advocacy communications.”
- Suggested rewrite:
- Enterprise web and content strategy
- Editorial governance and publishing operations
- Cross-channel digital operations leadership
- Public-sector, membership, and advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content planning

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- Avoid repeating “multi-channel communications” here if it already appears elsewhere; “operations leadership” adds more value.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill mix, but this item is too tool-list-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize platform leadership and execution strengths tied to recent work, not repeat every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization” instead of listing multiple CMSs first.
- Prioritize recent, differentiating strengths: Drupal, CMS modernization, API/integration work, workflow automation, AI-enabled search.
- Trim lower-signal or older items here; move/leave detailed tools like jQuery, SharePoint, Power Pages, Airtable in “Technical + IT.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • AI-enabled search and structured content experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; avoid repeating full tool inventories in both places.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies, so keep wording tighter or vary it slightly.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a generic inventory. Tighten it to emphasize strategic analytics capability and avoid repeating the more detailed “Technical + IT” section.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing: “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization” rather than only platform names.
- Use grouped wording for concision: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity.”
- Replace weaker items with stronger business-facing language: change “Leadership reporting” to “executive dashboards and decision support.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy and KPI design • Executive dashboards and decision support • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • SEO, UX insight and performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills higher-level and let Technical + IT hold the full tool list.
- “Performance analysis” overlaps with broader analytics language; “performance optimization” is sharper and more outcome-oriented.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Video production and editing

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and older NACo experience. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and make the phrasing more senior and specific.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, grouped phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same exact phrasing
- “Studio operations” and “Livestream studio workflows” are also echoed in Technical + IT, so this item should stay outcome-/capability-focused, not tool-focused

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” It should emphasize platform depth and recency—especially Drupal—rather than read like a duplicate tool list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show level of use: **Drupal (enterprise modernization, microsites, structured content)** • **WordPress** • **SharePoint** • **Power Pages** • **GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, prioritize by relevance/recency: put **Drupal** first and consider dropping **GitHub Pages** if it’s not materially important to recent roles.
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** or **CMS Platforms** for tighter phrasing.
- If you want more impact, add qualifiers instead of just names: e.g., **Drupal 10**, **enterprise SharePoint**, **campaign microsites**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep one as a concise platform list and the other focused on broader capabilities.
- Avoid repeating “CMS modernization” here since it already appears in Topline Skills.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools actually supporting recent Drupal, analytics, and automation work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for specificity and consistency: “HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • REST/API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions (CI/CD)”
- Drop version numbers unless they matter operationally; “HTML5/CSS3” feels dated and adds little value.
- Consider grouping by function for faster scanning: “Front-end: HTML/CSS, JavaScript/jQuery | Integration: REST/API integrations, GTM | DevOps/Edge: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “front-end implementation for Drupal” or “deployment automation,” rather than more tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere; avoid expanding this item into automation tools already covered in its own section.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Since “workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more clearly framed around orchestration tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by strongest/relevant tools first: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp**
- If space allows, add light functional grouping for clarity: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/workflow:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If you’ve built meaningful automations, consider replacing one lower-value tool with scope language, e.g. **Airtable workflow systems • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases here.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; keep them only if they support the workflow-systems positioning.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful platforms to include, but this item is too bare and undersells a clear strength shown in recent roles: enterprise email operations and audience engagement. It should read as a capability area, not just a software list.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely relevance/recency and standardize naming: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in brief parentheticals to signal depth: **Higher Logic (newsletter operations, audience segmentation)** • **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys (campaign automation)** • **Mailchimp (email production)**
- If you have metrics tied to these tools, move them into recent NACo bullets instead of here; keep this section tool-focused and concise.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” and NACo email/newsletter bullets; avoid adding generic phrases like “email strategy” here unless tied to platform use.
- Don’t repeat analytics/reporting language already covered under “Data, Analytics & Optimization.”

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Emphasize “firsts,” team-building, and concrete outputs, while trimming generic workflow language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: website refresh scale, livestream/event volume, video cadence, audience growth, or team support.
- Tighten phrasing and make contributions more active: “supported the creation” → “helped build”; “high-impact digital content” → specific formats and frequency.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving coordination across web, email, social and multimedia. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; if kept here, distinguish this as launching or initially producing the series.
- “strengthening workflows” is repeated elsewhere; use “helped establish early digital production processes” instead.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around concrete ownership and outputs, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and initiative: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams.”
- Make the podcast achievement the lead proof point: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Condense the rest into one supporting clause: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support research, member engagement and policy communications.”
- If possible, add one metric or output count: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, or audiences/stakeholders served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on research/program support plus the podcast launch.
- Avoid broad “policy work” phrasing unless you can specify the function or result.
